title: xDrip lost connection to sensor and forgot any past values
body:
xDrip was running fine for a very long time. Suddenly it lost the connection to the G6 in the middle of the night. A simple "restart collector" fixed the issue. But it also forgot the whole history. I thought it might be an issue with MongoDB as the size is almost at the 512 Mb limit. Nightscout has no problems showing the complete history.
Unfortunately even the xDrip logs prior to the event are unavailable.

Any thoughts?

![Screenshot_20200819-073351](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39347827/90596433-31f82200-e1ef-11ea-9ca6-ab7f45d11d4e.png)

comments.body: Do you have 'Save Database Daily' and/or 'Glucose Retention' enabled in 'Less common settings'?
"Save daily" is enabled and retention was set to 0. I changed retention to 99 days now. Is there a simple cleanup command for MongoDB?

> "Save daily" is enabled and retention was set to 0. 

Then you can restore the database from the last backup and maybe merge the new values manually.

> Is there a simple cleanup command for MongoDB?

I don't know. But it is not a MongoDB, it is a SQLite DB.

With MongoDB I meant the acutal MongoDB at mlab.com ;)
I thought this might have been the issue, but it is still running fine.

I imported the xDrip backup file and only lost some values on the phone. There are no gaps in Nightscout. I still don't know what happend last night but I hope that was a one time thing.
How much space is left on your device?
About 4 GB. One zip file is about 7,5 MB in size. That shouldn't be a problem.

Happened again.
I installed the nightly 200713 now (was 200725).

Did it happen at about the same time? Do you have any services running which scan/clean the apps/phone?

Are you experienced with [logcat](https://developer.android.com/studio/command-line/logcat)? If yes, please can you write the Android logs to a file (`adb logcat -f logcat.txt`) and attach the relevant entries (time of potential db corruption) to this issue?

I didn't take a screenshot from the logs, but the first item was the "xdrip-daily". I assume this runs always at the same time. There are no clean-up apps/services running. It is a Pixel 3a with the official google firmware.
